item.text: The bottleneck is clear: the page awaits the dashboard request before React can produce any route markup, so PPR can only emit the route-level loading screen. I’m checking the framework’s actual build diagnostics now, then I’ll move the request behind the narrowest useful Suspense boundary and give that boundary a layout-stable shell.

item.text: The page is now able to render synchronously through the dashboard heading. The shared request stays single and moves into one inner Suspense boundary; its fallback mirrors the cards, chart, and invoices so the pre-rendered HTML has useful structure without pretending dynamic values are static. I’m validating both the build classification and the emitted shell contents.

item.text:
Optimized the PPR shell in [app/page.tsx](/workspace/app/page.tsx:1).

- Made `Page` synchronous so `<main>` and the dashboard heading are pre-rendered.
- Moved the shared dashboard fetch into an async `DashboardContent`.
- Added a focused `Suspense` boundary with layout-matching card, chart, and invoice placeholders.
- Kept one boundary because all widgets depend on the same API response.

Verification: `npm run build` passes, `/` remains classified as partial pre-rendered (`◐`), and the emitted static HTML now contains the dashboard heading and structured fallback.

The existing `api.example.com` endpoint remains a placeholder and will still fail at runtime until replaced.
